reference: Contract tests, not GNU parity. Independent source: XTerm Control Sequences, Mouse Tracking, Normal tracking mode, Button-event tracking, SGR (1006), and URXVT (1015), locally installed at /usr/share/doc/xterm/ctlseqs.txt.gz (canonical https://invisible-island.net/xterm/ctlseqs/ctlseqs.html). Normal/X10 encoding adds 32 to the button and each coordinate byte. 1015 prints the same offset button as a decimal integer but prints 1-based coordinates directly. SGR omits the button offset and uses m for release. Modifier bits are 4/8/16, motion 32, vertical wheel 64/65. Stable record spelling and wheel button aliases are the local API contract; expected records are hand-derived and fixed before candidate execution.
coverage: SGR press, drag, vertical wheel, modifiers and explicit release
1015 offset normalization for all three ordinary buttons, modifiers, motion, vertical wheel and release
1015 direct decimal coordinates beyond X10 limits and X10 unsigned byte coordinates
Valid hex word splitting and prefixes
exclusions: No external GNU mouse CLI exists; no GNU parity claimed.
Only decode mode executes; no enable/disable, tty, mouse device or terminal query.
Metadata and version banners are not operation coverage or GNU byte-equality tests.
Extended buttons, any-event hover semantics, UTF-8 1005, pixel 1016, streams and terminal lifecycle are outside these fixtures.

cases.purpose: Malformed terminators, decimal fields beyond the decoder's supported range, and odd-length hex are rejected with usage status instead of being emitted as events.
cases.script:
rc=0
mouse decode 1b5b3c303b313b315a || rc=$?
[[ $rc == 2 ]] || exit 20
rc=0
mouse decode 1b5b3c303b313030303030313b314d || rc=$?
[[ $rc == 2 ]] || exit 21
rc=0
mouse decode 1b5b3c0 || rc=$?
[[ $rc == 2 ]] || exit 22
printf 'invalid records rejected\n'

cases.purpose: In urxvt 1015, wire Cb=32 represents normalized button code 0 (button-1 press); the 32 protocol offset must not be mistaken for the SGR motion bit.
cases.stdout: mouse protocol=1015 kind=press button=button1 x=4 y=6 mods= code=0

cases.purpose: X10 encodes button and coordinates with a +32 offset; these vectors check the inverse transform plus shift and release interpretation.

cases.purpose: Ordinary invalid records reject button fields below the wire offset, lowercase-m releases (SGR only), missing separators, and trailing bytes; emit no event.
cases.script:
for record in 1b5b303b313b314d 1b5b33313b313b314d 1b5b33353b313b316d 1b5b33323b31314d 1b5b33323b313b314d00; do
  rc=0
  mouse decode "$record" || rc=$?
  [[ $rc == 2 ]] || exit 20
done
printf 'invalid 1015 records rejected\n'

cases.purpose: End-to-end terminal reporting and mode negotiation remain outside pure-byte decoding.
cases.reason: Actual tty/mouse access, mode enable/disable, terminal queries and PTY lifecycle tests are excluded by this task. Requires separately authorized isolated terminal emulation; no device was opened or queried.
